sentences.text: Mr.Shobit Aditya, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Mr.Pramod Choubey, learned Government Advocate for the  respondent/State.
Heard.

sh This petition under section 482 of the Code of Criminal e Procedure has been filed to quash the extraordinary jurisdiction of this ad Court and to set aside the charge-sheet and criminal proceeding in Pr RCT No.13109/2010 pending before Special Magistrate, Bhopal under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
a hy 2.
The prosecution case, in brief, is that the authorized Food Inspector obtained a sample of food item 'mawa' (dry milk) from ad Ashirwad Mawa Kendra.
The petitioner is the proprietor of Ashirwad M Mawa Kendra.
On 12.10.2009, after observing all necessary formalities, the Food Inspector obtained the sample of 'mawa'.
One of of the sample was sent for analysis to the State Food Laboratory.
The rt other two parts were deposited before the Local Health Officer.
On ou 28.10.2009, the food item sent was found to be adulterated.

Prosecution was launched against the petitioner for violation of C sections 7(i), 7(iii) read with section 16(1)(a) of the Food Adulteration h Act, 1954 [hereinafter referred to as the "Act of 1954"] and Rule 50 of ig Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 [for short "Rules of H 1955"].
3.
On 10.1.2012 the petitioner-accused appeared before the trial Court.
He moved an application for sending the second sample to the Central Food Laboratory on 30.1.2012.
The sample was sent on 26.3.2012.
Report dated 22.9.2016 was received, in which, it is contended that the food item has been found to be putrefied and not fit for examination.
Therefore, the petitioner claimed that he was deprived of the provision under section 13(2) of the Act of 1954.
The petitioner also claimed that the prosecution did not file the criminal case in time.
The second sample could not be sent for examination to the Central Food Laboratory within time.
It is contended that milk products, as food items, are not fit for analysis after 10 months from the date of obtaining sample.
It is contended that purpose of section 13(2) of the Act of 1954 has been defeated claiming that it is a case of no evidence.
The petitioner claims that further proceeding in this regard would be abuse of process of the Court.

sentences.text: On behalf of the respondent/State the petition is vehemently opposed and it is contended that the delay was caused by the petitioner himself and, therefore, he cannot take advantage of his own mistake.
sh 5. Perused the record.
The Food Inspector has obtained the e sample on 10.12.2009 and sent for analysis of the first part on ad 24.10.2009.
The analysis of the State Food Laboratory has found that Pr the food item is adulterated.
However, when the second sample was sent for examination in the Central Food Laboratory, it was found that a the sample is unfit for examination.
The valuable right of the petitioner hy cannot be exercised.
ad 6. The petitioner's claim seems to be reasonable as the M second sample was sent to the Central Food Laboratory on 26.3.2012, which is after about two and half years.

It is observed that the milk of products gets deteriorated within 10 months from the date of collection, therefore, holding because of delay in the institution of the rt complainant, the valuable right of the petitioner has been infringed.

ou 7. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Municipal C Corporation of Delhi vs. Ghisaram, AIR 1967 SC 970 and in the case h of State of Harayana vs. Unique Farmaid P. Ltd. and others, AIR ig 2000 SCW 1985 has observed that the complaint filed as late as 19 H months and for this delay prosecution cannot thrust blame on the petitioner.

sentences.text: This delay is required to be explained by the prosecution.

But, even if they have genuine and reasonable explanation, the same will not help to them as it is settled legal proposition that milk and milk product like ice cream etc. gets deterioration within 10 months from the date of its lifting.
Meaning thereby, the sample may be fit for sending for further examination by the Central Food Laboratory within 10 months from the date of its collection by Food Inspector.
8. In the case of Ghisaram (supra) the same was sent after 19 months and, therefore, it was observed by the Apex Court that the accused has a right to apply under section 13(2) of the Act of 1954.
After the institution of the prosecution by the respondent and because of delay in institution of the complaint the valuable right of the petitioner has been infringed.
Thus, there seems to be no justification to allow the conduction of trial against the accused.

In the case of Unique Farmaid P.
Ltd. (supra) exercise of powers under section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure the Apex Court has quashed the proceeding pending against the accused.
10. In the present case also the complaint was filed on sh 02.12.2010 i.e. after about 1 (one) year and 2 (two) months.
After e appearance of the petitioner on 10.1.2012 the petitioner applied for ad sending the second sample on 30.1.2012.
The second sample was sent Pr to the Central Food Laboratory on 26.3.2012.
The report of the Central Food Laboratory was received on 22.2.2016 stating that the food a article is not fit for examination.

sentences.text: In the circumstances, the second sample was sent for ad examination after about 3 years.
Therefore, the important right of the M petitioner was infringed.
Hence, the case of the petitioner has been prejudiced.

In similar legal and factual circumstances, as available in of the present case, in the case of Suresh Narain vs. Food Inspector and another, 2003 (2) MPLJ 120 the proceedings of criminal case pending rt before the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Indore was quashed.

sentences.text: Similar ou finding has also been given in the case of Ravindra Agrawal vs. State C of Madhya Pradesh [M.Cr.C.No.4392/2017 decided on 20.9.2017].

sentences.text: h 12. For the reasons stated above, this petition succeeds.
It ig would be a futile exercise to allow the trial for the charges under H sections 7(i), 7(iii) read with section 16(1)(a) of the Act of 1954 and Rule 50 of Rules of 1955.
Accordingly, the criminal proceeding of RCT No.13109/2010 pending before Special Magistrate, Bhopal under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 is quashed.
